title: Enough K-injectives compute total right derived functors
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], and let $K(\mathcal A)$ be the homotopy category of its cochain complexes (morphisms are chain maps modulo chain homotopy), with localization $Q:K(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume every complex admits a quasi-isomorphism to a K-injective complex, where a complex $J$ is K-injective when every map from an acyclic complex to $J$ is homotopic to zero [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Let $\mathcal T$ be a triangulated category and $F:K(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal T$ an exact functor [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Then the total right derived functor $RF:D(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal T$ exists (with a natural transformation $\eta:F\to RF\circ Q$ such that composition with $\eta$ gives a bijection between natural transformations $RF\to G$ and $F\to G\circ Q$ for every functor $G:D(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal T$), and every K-injective complex $J$ computes it: the derived-functor comparison $F(J)\to RF(QJ)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 070K, Lemma lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies (literature/stacks-project/derived.tex); computation also Tag 070Y, lemma-K-injective-defined

proof.text: Use the concrete localization model of $D(\mathcal A)$ in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]: its objects are the complexes, and $Q$ changes the morphisms by inverting quasi-isomorphisms. For each complex $K$ choose, using the hypothesis, a quasi-isomorphism $u_K:K\to I_K$ with $I_K$ K-injective. Regard $u_K$ as a morphism in $K(\mathcal A)$ and put $q_K=Q(u_K)$, an isomorphism. These are objectwise choices; no functorial resolution is assumed. Set $RF(QK)=F(I_K)$.

source.place: Tag 070K, lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies; Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective (3); explicit construction and universal-property verification by the worker

proof.text: For a derived morphism $a:QK\to QL$, apply the Hom bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] with source $I_K$ and K-injective target $I_L$. It gives a unique $\widetilde a:I_K\to I_L$ in the homotopy category satisfying $Q(\widetilde a)=q_L\circ a\circ q_K^{-1}$. Define $RF(a)=F(\widetilde a)$. The lift of the identity is the identity, since its image is $q_Kq_K^{-1}$. For $b:QL\to QM$, $Q(\widetilde b\circ\widetilde a)=q_M\circ b\circ a\circ q_K^{-1}$, so uniqueness gives $\widetilde{b\circ a}=\widetilde b\circ\widetilde a$. Thus these choices define a functor on the entire derived category.

source.place: Tag 070K, lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies; Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective (3); explicit construction and universal-property verification by the worker

proof.text: Define $\eta_K=F(u_K):F(K)\to RF(QK)$. If $f:K\to L$ is a homotopy-category morphism, then $Q(\widetilde{Qf}\circ u_K)=q_L\circ Qf=Q(u_L\circ f)$. Injectivity of the Hom bijection in [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], now with source $K$ and target $I_L$, gives $\widetilde{Qf}\circ u_K=u_L\circ f$. Applying $F$ proves $RF(Qf)\circ\eta_K=\eta_L\circ F(f)$, so $\eta:F\to RF\circ Q$ is natural.

source.place: Tag 070K, lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies; Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective (3); explicit construction and universal-property verification by the worker

proof.text: Let $G:D(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal T$ be any functor and $\alpha:F\to G\circ Q$ any natural transformation. Define $\beta_{QK}=G(q_K^{-1})\circ\alpha_{I_K}:F(I_K)\to G(QK)$. For $a:QK\to QL$, naturality of $\alpha$ at $\widetilde a$ gives $\alpha_{I_L}\circ F(\widetilde a)=G(Q\widetilde a)\circ\alpha_{I_K}$. Substituting $Q\widetilde a=q_La q_K^{-1}$ yields $\beta_{QL}\circ RF(a)=G(a)\circ\beta_{QK}$. Naturality of $\alpha$ at $u_K$ also gives $\beta_{QK}\circ\eta_K=G(q_K^{-1})G(q_K)\alpha_K=\alpha_K$. This constructs a natural transformation $\beta:RF\to G$ whose composition with $\eta$ is $\alpha$.

source.place: Tag 070K, lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies; Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective (3); explicit construction and universal-property verification by the worker

proof.text: To prove uniqueness, observe that the lift defining $RF(q_K)$ is $u_{I_K}$: its image under $Q$ is $q_{I_K}\circ q_K\circ q_K^{-1}=q_{I_K}$, and [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] gives uniqueness with target $I_{I_K}$. Hence $RF(q_K)=F(u_{I_K})=\eta_{I_K}$. If $\gamma:RF\to G$ satisfies $\gamma_{QN}\circ\eta_N=\alpha_N$ for every $N$, its naturality at $q_K$ gives $G(q_K)\circ\gamma_{QK}=\gamma_{QI_K}\circ RF(q_K)=\gamma_{QI_K}\circ\eta_{I_K}=\alpha_{I_K}$. Since $G(q_K)$ is invertible, $\gamma_{QK}=G(q_K^{-1})\alpha_{I_K}=\beta_{QK}$. All derived objects occur as $QK$ in the chosen localization model. Thus composition with $\eta$ is the asserted bijection, with inverse $\alpha\mapsto\beta$.

source.place: Tag 070K, lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies; Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective (3); explicit construction and universal-property verification by the worker

proof.text: For a K-injective complex $J$, both $J$ and $I_J$ are K-injective and $u_J$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The last clause of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] makes $u_J$ a homotopy equivalence, hence an isomorphism in $K(\mathcal A)$. Applying the functor $F$ shows that $\eta_J=F(u_J):F(J)\to RF(QJ)$ is an isomorphism. This is exactly the derived-functor comparison constructed above. The existence and comparison clauses therefore hold for the stipulated exact $F$ (the universal-property construction itself needed only that $F$ is a functor).
